english.notes:
(i) This offence applies from 8th July 2026 due to the introduction of the designated body condition by the National Security (State Threats) Act 2026. This offence mirrors the structure of the previous offence but includes a designated body as well as a foreign power. For the offence applying before this date, see H101392.
(ii) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Attorney General, section 37 of the National Security Act 2023. (iii) This offence may be committed whether a person’s conduct takes place in the United Kingdom or elsewhere (section 2(4)), however conduct which takes place wholly outside the United Kingdom constitutes an offence only if the trade secret is in the possession or under the control of a UK person (section 2(5)).
(iv) This offence covers 'espionage' relating to the disclosure of trade secrets (information that has existing or potential commercial, economic or industrial value, such as a new technology developed in the UK). For the offence relating to the obtaining or disclosing of protected information relating to sensitive government information, see H102840. For the offence relating to assisting a foreign intelligence service, see H101393 (conduct 'intended' to assist) and H101394 (conduct 'likely to assist').
(v) The person's conduct must either meet the "foreign power condition" as set out in section 31 or the “designated body condition” in section 33B.
(vi) Additional powers of entry, search and seizure are provided in Schedule 2 where there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that this offence has been, or is about to be, committed.
